title: Smallest Odd Abundant Number: 945
content:
A natural number $n$ is **abundant** when $\sigma(n) > 2n$, where $\sigma(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} d$. The smallest abundant number is $12$, but the abundant numbers $12, 18, 20, 24, 30, \dots$ are all **even** for a while: the smallest **odd** abundant number is $945 = 3^3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$, with $\sigma(945) = 40 \cdot 6 \cdot 8 = 1920 > 1890 = 2 \cdot 945$.

The goal is `IsLeast {n \mid \text{Odd } n \wedge n.\text{Abundant}} 945$. The minimality half is a bounded check $\forall n < 945,\ \text{Odd } n \to \neg\, n.\text{Abundant}$. The obstruction is purely computational: Mathlib's `Nat.Abundant` is decidable only via `Finset`/`Multiset` divisor folds, whose **kernel** reduction blows up well before $945$, so a direct `decide` is infeasible. Keeping the proof axiom-free (kernel `decide`, not `native_decide`) requires a divisor sum the kernel can actually evaluate.

title: A Kernel-Reducible Divisor Sum
content: `sigmaAux n m` computes $\sum_{d=1}^{m} (d \text{ if } d \mid n \text{ else } 0)$ by **structural recursion on $m$**, and `sigmaFast n := sigmaAux n n`. The key design choice: no `Finset` or `Multiset` appears at reduction time, so the Lean kernel evaluates $\sigma$ through ordinary GMP-accelerated $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic. This is what makes the $n < 945$ check feasible by kernel `decide` where the canonical `Finset`-based representation cannot reduce.

title: Agreement with Mathlib's σ
content: `sigmaAux_eq_sum` (induction on $m$) identifies the recursion with the indicator sum over `range (m+1)`. `sigmaFast_eq_sigma` then uses `Finset.sum_filter` and the fact that $d \mid n$ with $n \neq 0$ forces $1 \le d \le n$ to collapse the filtered range to `n.divisors`, proving $\texttt{sigmaFast } n = \sum_{d \mid n} d$. After this one-time bridge, downstream reasoning may freely use the kernel-fast form.

title: Bounded Kernel decide and Minimality
content: `abundant_iff_sigmaFast` restates abundance as $2n < \texttt{sigmaFast } n$ (via `Nat.sum_divisors_eq_sum_properDivisors_add_self` and `omega`), and `abundant_945` follows from $\texttt{sigmaFast } 945 = 1920$. The minimality lower bound `not_abundant_odd_below_945 : ∀ n < 945, Odd n → sigmaFast n ≤ 2n` is a **single kernel `decide`** (`Nat.decidableBallLT`): even $n$ are discharged instantly because $\text{Odd } n$ is false, and odd $n$ reduce `sigmaFast n` in the kernel. `smallest_odd_abundant` assembles odd-abundance of $945$ with the lower bound — entirely axiom-free, with no `Lean.ofReduceBool`.
